explanations.explanation: This feature fires on structural “wrapper” lines and tokens that mark off or label sections of a text—e.g. horizontal rules or delimiters (====, ----), copyright/license headers in code comments, Q:/A: markers in Q&A posts, and section headings/metadata lines in wikis (References, Category:, See also, External links, etc.).

This feature detects the subword “Maz-” (a capital M followed by a-z-z), which almost always appears at the start of proper nouns—people’s names (Mazen, Mazie, Mazurek), place names (Mazandaran, Mazraeh-yeh), and brand names (Mazda)—serving as a reusable token fragment for those kinds of words.

This neuron fires on tokens used to declare file- or document-level metadata – e.g. PHP docblock annotations (@version, @package, @license, defined('_JEXEC')), Python/Unix shebangs and “coding:utf-8” lines, XML/HTML prologues (`<?xml … encoding="utf-8"?>`, `<resources>`, `<layout>` etc.), and similar top-of-file markup.
This feature fires on capitalized tokens marking the beginnings of named entities—proper names, place names, acronyms, paper titles, etc.

This neuron is essentially a character‐trigram detector for “bra,” firing on any token that contains that three‐letter sequence (e.g. words like bravery/braved, braising, brazenly, braid, braai, sports bra, etc.).

This neuron is essentially a character-n-gram detector: it lights up whenever a token contains certain 4–6-letter letter sequences (often common suffixes like “anch,” “rug,” “amine,” “ylate,” “uron,” “turn,” “ilis,” etc.), regardless of the word’s meaning.

This neuron fires on subword fragments that occur almost exclusively inside named entities—brand names, place names, personal names, org names or technical terms. It effectively flags “this token is part of a proper‐noun or other named‐entity.”
This feature fires on tokens wrapped in Markdown strong‐emphasis markers (i.e. the first subword inside a “**…**” bold span).
This feature fires on tokens that start a proper‐name or named‐entity string—i.e. the capitalized (or transliterated) prefix marking the beginning of people, places, organizations, etc.

This neuron fires on tokens that introduce new structural blocks or declarations—e.g. headings or front-matter delimiters (---, #), metadata keys (title:, parameters:), import/namespace declarations, XML/HTML tags, doc-comment starts, category/section labels, etc.
